claim: AmTrac and MepTrac are genetically encoded, single-fluorophore-based sensors that monitor membrane transporter activity in vivo.
source: We recently described a series of genetically encoded, single-fluorophore-based sensors, termed AmTrac and MepTrac, which monitor membrane transporter activity in vivo (De Michele et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to De Michele et al., 2013, which is the prior work describing these sensors.

claim: AmTrac and MepTrac are intensiometric sensors, which limits their use for quantitative studies.
source: However, being intensiometric, AmTrac and Meptrac are limited in their use for quantitative studies.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of intensiometric sensors, drawing on established knowledge about sensor types.

claim: Photophysical properties of different AmTrac sensors with diverging fluorescence properties were characterized using steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy as well as anisotropy decay analysis.
source: Here, we characterized the photophysical properties (steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy as well as anisotropy decay analysis) of different AmTrac sensors with diverging fluorescence properties in order to generate improved, ratiometric sensors.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental methods used to characterize the sensors.

claim: A set of dual-emission AmTrac sensors named deAmTracs was constructed by replacing key amino acid residues in AmTrac.
source: By replacing key amino acid residues in AmTrac we constructed a set of dual-emission AmTrac sensors named deAmTracs.
evidence: The manuscript describes the construction of new sensor variants.

claim: deAmTracs show opposing changes of blue and green emission with almost doubled emission ratio upon ammonium addition.
source: deAmTracs show opposing changes of blue and green emission with almost doubled emission ratio upon ammonium addition.
evidence: This is a direct observation from experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The response ratio of the deAmTracs correlated with transport activity in mutants with altered capacity.
source: The response ratio of the deAmTracs correlated with transport activity in mutants with altered capacity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing mutants with different transport activities.

claim: Partial disruption of distance-dependent excited-state proton transfer is important for the successful generation of single-fluorophore-based dual-emission sensors.
source: Our results suggest that partial disruption of distance-dependent excited-state proton transfer is important for the successful generation of single-fluorophore-based dual-emission sensors.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results, representing an inference from the data.

claim: AmTrac and MepTrac are composed of a circularly permuted enhanced green fluorescent protein (cpEGFP) inserted into the central loop of plant or yeast AMT/MEP ammonium transporters.
source: Both AmTrac and MepTrac are composed of a circularly permuted enhanced green fluorescent protein (cpEGFP) inserted into the central loop of plant or yeast AMT/MEP ammonium transporters.
evidence: This describes the structural composition of the sensors, which is established knowledge from prior work.

claim: AmTrac and MepTrac accurately report transporter activity as 30–50% fluorescence intensity decrease of green fluorescence.
source: Quantitative fluorescence spectroscopy of yeast cells expressing the sensor variants demonstrates that they accurately report transporter activity as 30–50% FI decrease of green FI (De Michele et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work and represents quantitative data.

claim: Ratiometric signal output would be clearly advantageous for sensor calibration and reliable quantitative imaging.
source: However, ratiometric signal output would be clearly advantageous for sensor calibration and reliable quantitative imaging (Tantama et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tantama et al., 2012, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Only a few existing single fluorescent protein sensors are ratiometric, displaying two emission maxima at a single excitation wavelength.
source: Only a few existing single FP sensors are ratiometric, displaying two emission maxima at a single excitation wavelength.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, representing established knowledge.

claim: The pH-sensors deGFP1 and deGFP4 and the calcium sensor GEM-GECO1 are single fluorescent protein sensors that are ratiometric.
source: The pH-sensors deGFP1 and deGFP4 (Hanson et al., 2002) and the calcium sensor GEM-GECO1 (Zhao et al., 2011) belong to this category.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hanson et al., 2002 and Zhao et al., 2011.

claim: AmTrac has similar steady-state fluorescence spectra to deGFP1 and deGFP4.
source: Based on similar steady-state fluorescence spectra of AmTrac and deGFP1 and deGFP4 (Hanson et al., 2002), we reasoned that it should be possible to turn AmTrac into a ratiometric, dual-emission sensor.
evidence: This is an observation from spectroscopic data and a citation to prior work.

claim: In AmTrac, the cpEGFP was inserted between residue 233 and 234 of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AtAMT1;3.
source: In AmTrac, the cpEGFP was inserted between residue 233 and 234 of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AtAMT1;3 (Figure 1A, top).
evidence: This describes the structural design of AmTrac, supported by Figure 1A.

claim: The AmTrac sensors differ only by two residues at the N-terminus of the cpEGFP, also referred to as left linker.
source: The AmTrac sensors differ only by two residues at the N-terminus of the cpEGFP, also referred to as left linker, the right linker being composed of phenylalanine (F) and asparagine (N) in all sensors.
evidence: This describes the structural differences between AmTrac variants.

claim: AmTrac-LE carries leucine (L, Leu234) and glutamate (E, Glu235) in the left linker.
source: The first AmTrac engineered, also named AmTrac-LE, carries leucine (L, Leu234) and glutamate (E, Glu235) in the left linker.
evidence: This describes the amino acid composition of a specific AmTrac variant.

claim: Brighter versions of AmTrac carry a serine (S, Ser235) in the second position of the left linker, and variable amino acids in the first position.
source: Brighter versions carry a serine (S, Ser235) in the second position of the left linker, and variable amino acids in the first position.
evidence: This describes the structural features of brighter AmTrac variants.

claim: AmTrac-GS carries a glycine (G, Gly234) in the first position of the left linker.
source: AmTrac-GS carries a glycine (G, Gly234)
evidence: This describes the amino acid composition of AmTrac-GS.

claim: AmTrac-LS carries a leucine (L, Leu234) in the first position of the left linker.
source: AmTrac-LS a leucine (L, Leu234)
evidence: This describes the amino acid composition of AmTrac-LS.

claim: AmTrac-IS carries an isoleucine (I, Ile234) in the first position of the left linker.
source: AmTrac-IS an isoleucine (I, Ile234) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the amino acid composition of AmTrac-IS, supported by Figure 1A.

claim: AmTrac-GS, -LS, -IS and -LE differ greatly in the shape and intensities of their fluorescence spectra when expressed in yeast.
source: Despite the minimal differences in their amino acid sequence, AmTrac-GS, -LS, -IS and LE differ greatly in the shape and intensities of their fluorescence spectra, when expressed in yeast (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental fluorescence spectroscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The fluorescence spectra of all AmTracs show two excitation maxima, at λexc ∼390 nm and λexc ∼500 nm, also referred to as A- and B-band.
source: The fluorescence spectra of all AmTracs show two excitation maxima, at λexc ∼390 nm and λexc ∼500 nm, also referred to as A- and B-band hereafter.
evidence: This is a direct observation from spectroscopic data.

claim: In AmTrac-LE, the A-state dominates the fluorescence spectrum.
source: In AmTrac-LE, the A-state dominates the fluorescence spectrum, whereas all other AmTracs (-GS, -LS and -IS) show an equilibrium shift toward the B-state.
evidence: This is an observation from spectroscopic data comparing different AmTrac variants.

claim: All AmTracs except AmTrac-LE show an equilibrium shift toward the B-state.
source: In AmTrac-LE, the A-state dominates the fluorescence spectrum, whereas all other AmTracs (-GS, -LS and -IS) show an equilibrium shift toward the B-state.
evidence: This is an observation from spectroscopic data.

claim: In wild type GFP, the A-band derives from the A-state, the protonated chromophore, while the B-state indicates the deprotonated chromophore.
source: In wild type GFP (wtGFP) (44), the A-band derives from the A-state, the protonated chromophore, while the B-state indicates the deprotonated chromophore (43).
evidence: This is established knowledge about GFP photophysics, supported by citations.

claim: Both A-state and B-state are coupled by a protonation equilibrium in both wtGFP and the AmTrac sensors.
source: Both states are coupled by a protonation equilibrium in both wtGFP and the AmTrac sensors.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge of GFP and observations of AmTrac.

claim: The generally accepted mechanism of single-fluorescent protein sensors assumes changes in the solvent accessibility and consequent quenching of the fluorescence.
source: The generally accepted mechanism of single-FP sensors assumes changes in the solvent accessibility and consequent quenching of the fluorescence (Akerboom et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: AmTracs are substantially different from the soluble sensors characterized so far.
source: However, AmTracs are substantially different from the soluble sensors characterized so far.
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on the structural differences of AmTracs.

claim: Membrane localization of the sensors reduces motion and mobility.
source: Membrane localization of the sensors reduces motion and mobility.
evidence: This is an inference based on the physical properties of membrane-bound proteins.

claim: Time-resolved fluorescence measurements were performed to detect if non-radiative processes such as solvent quenching or homo-FRET are involved in the sensor response.
source: Therefore, we performed time-resolved fluorescence measurements to detect if non-radiative processes such as solvent quenching or homo-FRET are involved in the sensor response.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used to investigate the sensor mechanism.

claim: AmTrac-GS showed single exponential decay kinetics with lifetime values of τ = 2.55 ± 0.04 ns when treated with water.
source: AmTrac-GS showed single exponential decay kinetics with lifetime values of τ = 2.55 ± 0.04 ns and τ = 2.48 ± 0.1 ns when treated with water and ammonium, respectively (Figure 1C top and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from time-resolved fluorescence measurements.

claim: AmTrac-GS showed single exponential decay kinetics with lifetime values of τ = 2.48 ± 0.1 ns when treated with ammonium.
source: AmTrac-GS showed single exponential decay kinetics with lifetime values of τ = 2.55 ± 0.04 ns and τ = 2.48 ± 0.1 ns when treated with water and ammonium, respectively (Figure 1C top and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from time-resolved fluorescence measurements.

claim: The lifetime values of AmTrac-GS are in agreement with most reports on a single lifetime of about τ = 2.5 to 2.8 ns for EGFP in solution.
source: These values are in agreement with most reports on a single lifetime of about τ = 2.5 to 2.8 ns for EGFP in solution (Stepanenko et al., 2004; Arpino et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison to established literature values, supported by citations.

claim: AmTrac-LE showed bi-exponential decay kinetics with fluorescence decay times of τ1 = 1.96 ± 0.4 ns and τ2 = 3.98 ± 0.32 ns when treated with water.
source: AmTrac-LE showed bi-exponential decay kinetics with fluorescence decay times of τ1 = 1.96 ± 0.4 ns and τ2 = 3.98 ± 0.32 ns and τ1 = 1.69 ± 0.07 ns and τ2 = 3.96 ± 0.17 ns when treated with water or ammonium, respectively (Figure 1C bottom and Figure 1—figure supplements 1, 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from time-resolved fluorescence measurements.

claim: AmTrac-LE showed bi-exponential decay kinetics with fluorescence decay times of τ1 = 1.69 ± 0.07 ns and τ2 = 3.96 ± 0.17 ns when treated with ammonium.
source: AmTrac-LE showed bi-exponential decay kinetics with fluorescence decay times of τ1 = 1.96 ± 0.4 ns and τ2 = 3.98 ± 0.32 ns and τ1 = 1.69 ± 0.07 ns and τ2 = 3.96 ± 0.17 ns when treated with water or ammonium, respectively (Figure 1C bottom and Figure 1—figure supplements 1, 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from time-resolved fluorescence measurements.

claim: The two lifetime components found for AmTrac-LE are indicative of the presence of two species in the excited state.
source: The two lifetime components found for AmTrac-LE are indicative of the presence of two species in the excited state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the bi-exponential decay data.

claim: The response mechanism of AmTrac-LE vs -GS differs with regard to which state (A- or B-state) is excited.
source: We thus conclude that the response mechanism of AmTrac-LE vs -GS differs with regard to which state (A- or B-state) is excited, and postulate that either different excited state reactions and/or different excited state species are involved.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differences in decay kinetics between the two sensors.

claim: External quenching effects due to altered solvent access are excluded as the mechanism in AmTracs.
source: Since the lifetime values in absence and presence of ammonium differed, at most, by less than 1 ns for AmTrac-LE and -GS (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) we exclude external quenching effects due to altered solvent access in AmTracs, which is the widely accepted mechanism of single-FP sensors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the small changes in lifetime values upon ammonium treatment.

claim: The distance of the cpEGFP moieties in the sensors allows for homo-FRET.
source: The distance of the cpEGFP moieties in the sensors allows for homo-FRET, but anisotropy decay kinetics changed only minimally in the presence of ammonium for AmTrac-GS and -LE (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural arrangement of the sensors.

claim: Anisotropy decay kinetics changed only minimally in the presence of ammonium for AmTrac-GS and -LE.
source: The distance of the cpEGFP moieties in the sensors allows for homo-FRET, but anisotropy decay kinetics changed only minimally in the presence of ammonium for AmTrac-GS and -LE (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is an observation from anisotropy decay measurements.

claim: The fluorescence intensity decrease is not the result of a change in the efficiency of homo-FRET.
source: We thus conclude that the FI decrease is not the result of a change in the efficiency of (a possible) homo-FRET and postulate that structural rearrangements affect the protonation states and thus the FI.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the anisotropy decay data.

claim: Structural rearrangements affect the protonation states and thus the fluorescence intensity in AmTracs.
source: We thus conclude that the FI decrease is not the result of a change in the efficiency of (a possible) homo-FRET and postulate that structural rearrangements affect the protonation states and thus the FI.
evidence: This is a postulated mechanism based on the experimental observations.

claim: Excitation of the A-state of wtGFP leads to green emission due to excited-state proton transfer (ESPT).
source: Excitation of the A-state of wtGFP leads to green emission due to excited-state proton transfer (ESPT) (Chattoraj et al., 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge about wtGFP photophysics, supported by a citation.

claim: ESPT in wtGFP is a photophysical phenomenon that describes the rapid deprotonation of the neutral chromophore in the excited state leading to loss of blue fluorescence and formation of a green-emitting intermediate state (I-state).
source: ESPT in wtGFP is a photophysical phenomenon that describes the rapid deprotonation of the neutral chromophore in the excited state leading to loss of blue fluorescence and formation of a green-emitting intermediate state (I-state).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the ESPT mechanism in GFP.

claim: The proton travels from the chromophore hydroxyl group, via a buried water molecule and neighboring side chain serine 205 (Ser205), to the final acceptor Glu222 after excitation of the A-form in wtGFP.
source: The proton travels from the chromophore hydroxyl group, via a buried water molecule and neighboring side chain serine 205 (Ser205), to the final acceptor Glu222 after excitation of the A-form.
evidence: This describes the established ESPT pathway in wtGFP.

claim: ESPT is usually prevented in EGFP due to the S65T mutation.
source: ESPT is usually prevented in EGFP due to the S65T mutation (Brejc et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge about EGFP, supported by a citation.

claim: Green fluorescence was detected after excitation of the A-state in AmTrac-LE and -GS, supporting the hypothesis of ESPT occurrence.
source: To test for ESPT in AmTracs, we recorded fluorescence emission spectra of yeast transformed with AmTrac-LE and -GS after excitation of the A-state (λexc 395 nm), in presence of varying ammonium concentrations. Green fluorescence was detected, further supporting the hypothesis of ESPT occurrence (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from fluorescence spectroscopy experiments.

claim: AmTrac-LE failed to fully respond to ammonium treatment when the A-state was excited, since the fluorescence intensity decreased by 30% only.
source: However, AmTrac-LE failed to fully respond to ammonium treatment when the A-state was excited, since the FI decreased by 30% only (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from fluorescence measurements.

claim: When the B-state was excited in AmTrac-LE, the fluorescence intensity decreased up to ∼50%.
source: Conversely, when the B-state was excited, the FI decreased up to ∼50% (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from fluorescence measurements.

claim: The emission spectrum of AmTrac-LE was characterized by two emission maxima: one higher energy shoulder-like maximum at λem 490 nm and a distinct peak at λem 515 nm when the A-state was excited.
source: The emission spectrum of AmTrac-LE was characterized by another unique feature: the excitation of the A-state showed two emission maxima, one higher energy shoulder-like maximum at λem 490 nm and a distinct peak at λem 515 nm.
evidence: This is a direct observation from spectroscopic data.

claim: Upon ammonium addition, the relative intensity of the peaks was altered and an iso-emissive point was observed in AmTrac-LE.
source: Upon ammonium addition, the relative intensity of the peaks was altered and an iso-emissive point was observed (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an observation from fluorescence spectroscopy experiments.

claim: The iso-emissive behavior was detected for AmTrac-LE but not for AmTrac-GS.
source: Interestingly, this iso-emissive behavior was detected for AmTrac-LE but not for AmTrac-GS (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a comparative observation from spectroscopic data.

claim: Crystal structures are not available yet for AmTrac sensors.
source: Crystal structures of AmTrac sensors are not available yet.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of structural knowledge.

claim: Crystal structures have been solved for cpEGFP, as free protein or within sensors.
source: However, crystal structures have been solved for cpEGFP, as free protein or within sensors (Wang et al., 2008; Akerboom et al., 2009; Leder et al., 2010) and can provide clues on how the linker residues are involved in the structural rearrangements during the sensing mechanism.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: The crystal structure of cpEGFP (PDB 3EVP) shows two rotamers for Glu148 in close proximity to the chromophore Thr65–Tyr66–Gly67.
source: The crystal structure of cpEGFP (PDB 3EVP) shows two rotamers for Glu148 in close proximity to the chromophore Thr65–Tyr66–Gly67, which indicates a high degree of flexibility at position 148.
evidence: This is an observation from structural data in the Protein Data Bank.

claim: The two rotamers for Glu148 indicate a high degree of flexibility at position 148 in cpEGFP.
source: The crystal structure of cpEGFP (PDB 3EVP) shows two rotamers for Glu148 in close proximity to the chromophore Thr65–Tyr66–Gly67, which indicates a high degree of flexibility at position 148.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: Due to re-arrangements in the cpEGFP barrel, Glu148 may exist in different orientations and distances to the phenyl-group of the chromophore.
source: We assume that due to re-arrangements in the cpEGFP barrel, Glu148 may exist in different orientations and distances to the phenyl-group of the chromophore (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on structural analysis.

claim: Glu148 in cpEGFP corresponds to Glu235 in AmTrac-LE.
source: Since Glu148 corresponds to Glu235 in AmTrac-LE, we consider the solved structure of cpEGFP as a proxy for AmTrac-LE.
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence alignment and structural homology.

claim: Theoretical modifications of the linker sequence were performed using Pymol by replacing the linker residues LE of cpEGFP (PDB 3EVP) with GS.
source: Theoretical modifications of the linker sequence were performed using Pymol by replacing the linker residues LE of cpEGFP (PDB 3EVP) with GS.
evidence: This describes a computational modeling approach.

claim: The theoretical modification shows only one conformational state for serine of the GS linker.
source: The result shows only one conformational state for serine of the GS linker (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) indicating more stability during conformation changes.
evidence: This is a result from computational modeling.

claim: The single conformational state of the GS linker indicates more stability during conformation changes.
source: The result shows only one conformational state for serine of the GS linker (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) indicating more stability during conformation changes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the modeling results.

claim: Different amino acid linkers have an impact on the structural environment of the chromophore.
source: This also indicates the impact of different amino acid linkers on the structural environment of the chromophore.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling and spectroscopic data.

claim: Glu235 of AmTrac-LE relocates during the sensing process, most likely altering the efficiency of ESPT and in turn leading to blue and green fluorescence emission.
source: We postulate that Glu235 of AmTrac-LE relocates during the sensing process, most likely altering the efficiency of ESPT and in turn leading to blue and green fluorescence emission.
evidence: This is a postulated mechanism based on structural and spectroscopic data.

claim: The spectral behavior of AmTrac-LE shows similarities with the dual-emission pH sensor deGFP1.
source: The spectral behavior of AmTrac-LE shows similarities with the dual-emission pH sensor deGFP1 (Hanson et al., 2002) as well as the GFP mutant S65T/H148E (Shu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a comparative observation supported by citations.

claim: The spectral behavior of AmTrac-LE shows similarities with the GFP mutant S65T/H148E.
source: The spectral behavior of AmTrac-LE shows similarities with the dual-emission pH sensor deGFP1 (Hanson et al., 2002) as well as the GFP mutant S65T/H148E (Shu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a comparative observation supported by citations.

claim: The left linker amino acids were modified to generate improved dual-emission sensors with a larger ratio change compared to AmTrac-LE.
source: Therefore, we reasoned that it should be possible to generate improved dual-emission sensors with a larger ratio change compared to AmTrac-LE. We modified the left linker amino acids only, since they appeared to be involved in the dual-emission behavior.
evidence: This describes the experimental strategy for sensor engineering.

claim: LE was replaced with two random amino acids to check for all possible combinations.
source: We replaced LE with two random amino acids, to check for all possible combinations, and analyzed these constructs in yeast.
evidence: This describes the mutagenesis approach.

claim: Out of more than 500 yeast colonies screened, four candidates with the new linker composition CP, FP, RP, YP displayed distinct dual-emission patterns.
source: Out of more than 500 yeast colonies screened, we found four candidates with the new linker composition CP, FP, RP, YP that displayed distinct dual-emission patterns and two of these candidates showed improved ratios upon ammonium treatment.
evidence: This is a result from the screening experiment.

claim: Two of the four candidates showed improved ratios upon ammonium treatment.
source: Out of more than 500 yeast colonies screened, we found four candidates with the new linker composition CP, FP, RP, YP that displayed distinct dual-emission patterns and two of these candidates showed improved ratios upon ammonium treatment.
evidence: This is a result from the screening experiment.

claim: All four constructs named deAmTracs contained a proline residue at the linker position of the former Glu235.
source: Interestingly, all four constructs, named deAmTracs, contained a proline residue at the linker position of the former Glu235, while the first amino acid of the linker varied (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the screening results.

claim: The two candidates with the highest ratio changes are deAmTrac-CP and -FP.
source: The two candidates with the highest ratio changes, deAmTrac-CP and -FP, are described in more detail (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a result from the screening experiment.

claim: deAmTrac-CP carried a cysteine and proline in the left linker.
source: deAmTrac-CP carried a cysteine and proline, while deAmTrac-FP contained phenylalanine and proline in the left linker.
evidence: This describes the amino acid composition of deAmTrac-CP.

claim: deAmTrac-FP contained phenylalanine and proline in the left linker.
source: deAmTrac-CP carried a cysteine and proline, while deAmTrac-FP contained phenylalanine and proline in the left linker.
evidence: This describes the amino acid composition of deAmTrac-FP.

claim: Upon excitation with λexc 395 nm, blue and green emission maxima at 490 nm and 515 nm, respectively, were detected in deAmTrac-CP and -FP.
source: Upon excitation with λexc 395 nm, blue and green emission maxima at 490 nm and 515 nm, respectively, were detected, which showed opposing changes in FI upon ammonium treatment.
evidence: This is an observation from fluorescence spectroscopy.

claim: The blue and green emission maxima showed opposing changes in fluorescence intensity upon ammonium treatment in deAmTrac-CP and -FP.
source: Upon excitation with λexc 395 nm, blue and green emission maxima at 490 nm and 515 nm, respectively, were detected, which showed opposing changes in FI upon ammonium treatment.
evidence: This is an observation from fluorescence spectroscopy.

claim: A clear iso-emissive point in the dual-emission spectra was observed for deAmTrac-CP and -FP.
source: A clear iso-emissive point in the dual-emission spectra was observed (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an observation from fluorescence spectroscopy.

claim: The ratio values almost doubled for both deAmTrac-CP and -FP upon ammonium treatment.
source: Plotting the response ratio of the intensity of the A-state /I-state vs the external ammonium concentration showed that the ratio values almost doubled for both deAmTrac-CP and -FP (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from fluorescence measurements.

claim: The affinity constant from the response ratio towards ammonium for deAmTrac-CP is EC50 54 ± 9 µM.
source: The affinity constants from the response ratio towards ammonium for deAmTrac-CP (EC50 54 ± 9 µM) and deAmTrac-FP (EC50 36 ± 6 µM) were similar to AmTrac (EC50 55 ± 7 µM) (De Michele et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from dose-response analysis.

claim: The affinity constant from the response ratio towards ammonium for deAmTrac-FP is EC50 36 ± 6 µM.
source: The affinity constants from the response ratio towards ammonium for deAmTrac-CP (EC50 54 ± 9 µM) and deAmTrac-FP (EC50 36 ± 6 µM) were similar to AmTrac (EC50 55 ± 7 µM) (De Michele et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from dose-response analysis.

claim: The affinity constants of deAmTrac-CP and -FP were similar to AmTrac (EC50 55 ± 7 µM).
source: The affinity constants from the response ratio towards ammonium for deAmTrac-CP (EC50 54 ± 9 µM) and deAmTrac-FP (EC50 36 ± 6 µM) were similar to AmTrac (EC50 55 ± 7 µM) (De Michele et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a comparative result supported by data and citation.

claim: Proline or glutamic acid at position 235 are involved in hindering deprotonation or stabilizing the protonated state of the chromophore.
source: Due to the appearance of blue emission we speculate that proline or glutamic acid at position 235 are involved in hindering deprotonation or stabilizing the protonated state of the chromophore.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed blue emission.

claim: Theoretical modification of the LE linker in the crystal structure of cpEGFP (PDB 3EVP) for either CP or FP using Pymol yields different rotamers.
source: Theoretical modification of the LE linker in the crystal structure of cpEGFP (PDB 3EVP) for either CP or FP using Pymol yields different rotamers (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from computational modeling.

claim: The residues CP and FP allow for more flexibility due to the possibility of different conformational states.
source: We postulate that the residues CP and FP allow for more flexibility due to the possibility of different conformational states.
evidence: This is a postulate based on the modeling results.

claim: The linker residues CP and FP may partially disrupt the ESPT pathway, preventing rapid proton transfer and trapping the excited A-state which consequently emits blue light.
source: Differently from GS in AmTrac-GS, these linker residues may partially disrupt the ESPT pathway, preventing rapid proton transfer and trapping the excited A-state which consequently emits blue light.
evidence: This is a postulated mechanism based on the spectroscopic observations.

claim: The blue emission is rather small, since the green emission from successful ESPT dominates the spectrum.
source: The blue emission is rather small, since the green emission from successful ESPT dominates the spectrum.
evidence: This is an observation from the spectroscopic data.

claim: AmTrac's fluorescence response is strictly correlated to the ammonium transporter activity.
source: Several lines of evidence demonstrated that AmTrac's fluorescence response is strictly correlated to the ammonium transporter activity (De Michele et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion from prior work, supported by a citation.

claim: A series of mutants with altered transporter activity was generated based on the suppressor screen for the inactivating mutation T464D in AmTrac-LE.
source: To verify that such correlation was maintained in deAmTracs, we generated a series of mutants with altered transporter activity, based on the suppressor screen for the inactivating mutation T464D in AmTrac-LE (De Michele et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach, supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In deAmTrac-CP and -FP, the T464D mutation was sufficient to block growth and response.
source: In deAmTrac-CP and -FP, the T464D mutation was still sufficient to block growth and response.
evidence: This is an observation from growth and fluorescence assays.

claim: In the T464D mutant background, the presence of the suppressing mutation A141E increased the ratiometric response and transport capacity.
source: In the T464D mutant background the presence of the suppressing mutation A141E increased the ratiometric response and transport capacity, shown as reduced growth of the mutants on high ammonium concentrations.
evidence: This is an observation from growth and fluorescence assays.

claim: Mutation Q61E restored growth and response of deAmTrac-T464D, although not to the full extent.
source: Conversely, mutation Q61E restored growth and response of deAmTrac-T464D, although not to the full extent (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from growth and fluorescence assays.

claim: The mutations had an effect on transport activity and response similar to AmTrac-LE.
source: Overall, the mutations had an effect on transport activity and response similar to AmTrac-LE (De Michele et al., 2013) (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a comparative observation supported by data and citation.

claim: In the T464D mutant, the blue emission disappeared, and only green emission was detected.
source: Spectral analysis of the mutant deAmTracs showed the impact of the introduced mutations on the dual-emission pattern. In the T464D mutant the blue emission disappeared, and only green emission was detected.
evidence: This is an observation from spectroscopic analysis of mutants.

claim: In presence of A141E, blue emission increased and green emission decreased.
source: In presence of A141E, blue emission increased and green emission decreased.
evidence: This is an observation from spectroscopic analysis of mutants.

claim: Q61E shows the opposite effect with decreased blue and increased green emission at high ammonium concentrations.
